# Requested assets

Every image the app needs, with its size, the images to attach and a prompt to paste. **The images are generated with AI, outside the repo:** you paste each prompt into an AI image tool that takes reference images (ChatGPT or the GPT Image API), attach the listed images, and drop the result into the folder in its entry, named exactly as shown. Nothing in this repo or its pipeline calls an image model. Until an image arrives, the app and the previewer show a static placeholder from `content/placeholders/`.

**Each story is requested in its own file,** next to its folders (`content/stories/<id>/REQUESTED_ASSETS.md`, linked below), **with its own art style, style anchor and characters.** Stories don't share a style or a character unless a story's `bible.json` declares it: `styleFrom` to reuse another story's art style, `from` on a cast member or prop to reuse another story's character. This file is only the index, the method and the app's own images.

This file is generated. To change a request, edit the story's `bible.json`, `shots.json` or `style/style.json` (or `content/app/assets.json` and `content/app/style.json` for the app icon), then run `cd tools && uv run story assets`. Run it again after delivering files, and the ⬜ entries turn ✅. Narration is requested separately, per language: [REQUESTED_AUDIO.md](REQUESTED_AUDIO.md) is its index, and each story has one `audio/<lang>/REQUESTED_AUDIO.md` per language. The pictures are the same in every language.

## How to make them

Image models make every picture from scratch and drift from page to page; there's no switch that locks a character. This method keeps a story's cast and style the same on every page:

1. **Anchors first, per story.** In the story's file, make its style anchor, then its reference sheets (with the style anchor attached), and approve them before anything else: every later prompt of that story attaches them. Then the story's first batch, then the rest in the order listed.
2. **Attach the listed images, in the listed order.** The prompt starts by saying what each one is for ("Image 2 is the character reference for Mia"). A one-scene character without a sheet is described in words only.
3. **Paste the prompt as it is.** The style, palette, character and place descriptions are word for word the same in every prompt of a story; only the scene at the end changes. Small rewordings shift colors and proportions. To change a description, change its source and run `story assets`, so every prompt changes together.
4. **Edit, don't start over,** where an entry says *Edit from*: it's the same place, light and framing as an earlier picture, so edit that one (reply to it in ChatGPT, or send it to the image edit endpoint) and keep its background and light. Other pictures in a place already painted attach its first picture as the location reference.
5. **Build crowded scenes in layers.** With 4 or more named characters in one picture, faces and clothes bleed into each other. Those entries give the steps: the place first, then one character at a time, each with its reference attached. Use the same steps for any picture whose characters come out mixed up.
6. **Fix drift with a narrow edit,** not a new picture: attach the reference and say exactly what to change and what to keep ("Redraw only Tuck's scarf to match the attached reference image. Keep everything else exactly the same.").
7. **Never name an artist.** A style is described by medium and technique only.

## How to deliver

- **Name** each file after its asset id, as `.png`, `.webp` or `.jpg`. sRGB, no transparency, no watermark, no text.
- **Where**: each entry names its folder. A story's style anchor goes in its `style/` folder, its reference sheets in its `characters/` folder, everything else in its `images/` folder.
- **Size**: at least the minimum below, ideally the larger size. Packaging crops, resizes and converts to WebP, and strips metadata.
- **Order**: a story's style anchor, then its reference sheets. Every other picture of a character or prop must match its sheet.
- **Provenance**: note the tool and model that made each image in the story's `provenance.json`, and keep its terms (commercial use in an app) on file. The store listing says the pictures are made with AI.

| Kind | Aspect | Minimum | Ideal | Placeholder | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Style anchor | 4:3 landscape | 1600×1200 | 2400×1800 | `none` | Full bleed, no border or vignette. Only the place and its light: no people, animals or characters. |
| Reference sheet | 3:2 landscape | 2400×1600 | 3000×2000 | `sheet.svg` | Plain, light, even paper-colored background with flat, even light: no cast shadows, no scenery, no labels. Every view at the same scale, side by side, none overlapping. |
| Cover | 3:4 portrait | 1200×1600 | 1500×2000 | `cover.svg` | No title and no text of any kind: the app draws the title over the bottom quarter, so keep that area calm (grass, water, sky). Main characters in the upper two thirds. |
| Page illustration | 4:3 landscape | 1600×1200 | 2400×1800 | `page.svg` | Full bleed, no border or vignette. Keep the main action inside the middle 80%: the edges get cropped on some screens. |
| Ending illustration | 4:3 landscape | 1600×1200 | 2400×1800 | `page.svg` | Full bleed, no border. Keep the main action inside the middle 80%, and the key moment in the very center: a circle cropped from the middle becomes the ending's badge. |
| Choice card | 1:1 square | 768×768 | 1024×1024 | `card.svg` | One clear subject on a simple, calm background, readable as a small thumbnail (about 160 pt wide on a phone). |

## App images (proposed, not yet approved)

The app's own pictures, outside any story, in the app's own style (Gouache app icon, proposed, not yet approved, from `content/app/style.json`). Deliver them into `content/app/`. The Android launcher icon is built from the two layers, iOS and the stores use `app-icon`.

#### ✅ `app-icon`: App icon

- **File:** `content/app/app-icon.png`
- **Size:** 1:1 square, exactly 1024×1024 px
- **Attach:** nothing. Make this one first: the others are edits of it.

```text
Style: App icon painted in opaque, matte gouache on warm off-white paper, with a visible dry-brush texture and paper grain. One bold, chunky, rounded subject with a clear silhouette and almost no small details, so it reads at the size of a fingertip; flat areas of color, no outlines, edges made by color and value. One clear light idea: a warm gold glow with a soft halo against cool blues, never black.
Palette: paper #F3EAD8, cream #FFF6E3, night blue #2E3F66, twilight lilac #B9A3D0, meadow green #7FA65A, hedge green #3F6B4A, earth brown #8A5A3C, lantern gold #F6C453.

Never: any text: letters, numbers, signs, labels, logos, watermarks, signatures, musical notes; photorealism, 3D renders, glossy plastic or clay looks; black outlines, comic halftones, anime styling; pure black shadows, horror lighting, menacing silhouettes; sharp teeth, claws on display, angry or scary faces; extra or missing fingers, limbs, ears or tails; melted or merged shapes; real brands, real people, existing characters; copying the look of a named illustrator, an existing book or a studio.
Format: 1:1 square. PNG, opaque, square corners (the stores round them). The app's own style, simplified: big shapes that still read at 29 pt on a home screen. No text.

Subject: An open picture book seen from slightly above, its pages fanning up like wings, with a small round star glowing lantern gold rising out of the pages and lighting them warmly. Simple and bold enough to read at the size of a fingertip.
Background: Flat warm night blue with a faint dry-brush texture, a few tiny cream dots of stars far apart.
Must show: the open book, big and centered; the glowing star, the warmest and brightest spot.
Avoid here: characters from any story (the icon is the app, not one story); letters, words or numbers; rounded corners or a border: the stores round the corners themselves; transparency.
```
